0.long_answer: Hereditary spastic paraplegia can be inherited in different ways, but when the condition specifically affects males while females tend to be carriers, the inheritance pattern involved is X-linked recessive. In this pattern, because males have only one X chromosome, a single disease-causing mutation on that chromosome will result in the disorder. On the other hand, females have two X chromosomes, so if they carry one mutated gene, the normal copy on the other X chromosome usually prevents the full expression of the disorder, rendering them carriers.
